Summary

Concurrent MCP server discovery (startup or config reload) races on runtime creation: each server's \_ensureRegistered sees `this._runtime == null`, builds its own runtime, and overwrites the previous one. Servers registered on an overwritten instance are lost, and all later refreshes and tool calls for them fail instantly with `Unknown MCP server '<name>'`.

Environment

* getnao/nao:0.3.0 (Docker) — also reproduced after rebuild; the same code is in current main (apps/backend/src/services/mcp.ts)
* 3 stdio servers in agent/mcps/mcp.json (affects any config with ≥2 non-OAuth servers; transport-independent — one of ours is a plain stdio server, two use mcp-remote)

Reproduction

1. Configure 2+ servers in agent/mcps/mcp.json.
2. Start the container with no spec dirs under agent/mcps/ (forces parallel discovery), or touch mcp.json to trigger \_reloadAndDiscover.
3. Click refresh on a server in the MCP settings panel, or let the agent call one of its tools.
4. Some subset of servers fails with Unknown MCP server '' in \~30 ms. Which server fails varies per run (whoever's createRuntime() resolves last "wins").

Log signature: `[ERROR] [tool] MCP discovery failed: <name> / MCP tool call failed: <name>/<tool> with the error Unknown MCP server '<name>'.`

Root cause

\_ensureRegistered has a check-then-act race:

```
private async _ensureRegistered(name: string): Promise<void> {
    if (!this._runtime) {
        this._runtime = await createRuntime();   // N concurrent callers → N runtimes, last write wins
    }
    if (this._registered.has(name)) {
        return;                                  // sta a discarded runtime
    }
    ...
}

```

All parallel discoveries pass the !this.\_runtime check before any assignment resolves. Each registers its server on whichever instance is current at its own resolution time; \_registered accumulates all names, so subsequent calls skip re-registration and hit the surviving runtime, which never saw the definition.

Related: this code path replaced the per-call runtime from #202 (fixed in #1049) — same symptom, new mechanism.

Suggested fix

Memoize the in-flight createRuntime() so concurrent callers share one runtime

```
private _runtimePromise: Promise<Runtime> | null = null;

private async _ensureRegistered(name: string): Promise<void> {
    if (!this._runtime) {
        if (!this._runtimePromise) {
            this._runtimePromise = createRuntime().catc
                this._runtimePromise = null;
                throw error;
            });
        }
        this._runtime = await this._runtimePromise;
    }
    ...
}

```

Verified in our deployment: with this change, parallel rediscovery of all 3 servers completes cleanly and tool calls succeed; unpatched, at least one server fails every reload. Happy to send this as a PR.

## Where mine was wrong

Their PR description undersells the diff. The interesting part isn't the memoization — we both wrote essentially the same thing — it's commit `65cbce8`, which fixes a second-order race cubic flagged and I missed:

```ts
this._runtimePromise = createRuntime().catch((error) => {
    this._runtimePromise = null;   // clears whatever is current, not necessarily mine
    throw error;
});
...
this._runtime = await this._sharedRuntime();   // publishes unconditionally, even if stale
```

If `_reloadAndDiscover()` fires while a creation is in flight, `_resetRuntime()` nulls both fields, the reload starts creation R2, and then the *old* creation resolves and assigns `this._runtime = R1`. Split runtimes again — the original bug, reintroduced through a narrower window. Their version compares identity before both clearing and publishing, and loops so a caller whose creation was superseded re-awaits the current one.

I didn't want to take that on trust, so I added a third test that gates `createRuntime()` and interleaves a reload between two registrations. Against my implementation the surviving runtime holds only `beta`; `alpha` is stranded. Against theirs both land on the same runtime. Same failure shape as the original issue, so it's a real regression risk and not a theoretical one.

## Where mine adds something

The one thing my work has that the PR doesn't is the tests — their diff touches `mcp.ts` and nothing else. That matters more than usual here, because this is the third time this symptom has shipped: per-call runtime in #202, fixed in #1049, replaced by the shared-runtime race in #1292. A fix with no test is how it comes back a fourth time. The three tests I have now cover parallel startup discovery, tool calls after a botched discovery, and the reload-mid-creation case, and all three fail against `main`.

So the useful outcome isn't "ours vs theirs" — it's their `_ensureRegistered` plus my `mcp-runtime-race.test.ts`. That's the current state of the working tree: 3 tests passing, `npm run lint -w @nao/backend` clean.

## One thing neither of us fixes

`_resetRuntime()` drops the runtime with `this._runtime = null` and never calls `runtime.close()`, which is never called anywhere in the backend. By the time a reload happens the old runtime has live clients, and for stdio servers those are spawned child processes — so every `mcp.json` edit orphans one process per connected stdio server. beherap's setup (three stdio servers, two via `mcp-remote`) would leak three per reload. Out of scope for this PR, but probably worth its own issue.

Fixes #1292

When several MCP servers are discovered in parallel (startup or config reload), every `_ensureRegistered` call saw `_runtime == null`, built its own runtime, and overwrote the previous one. Servers registered on an overwritten instance were lost, so refreshes and tool calls failed with `Unknown MCP server '<name>'`.

This memoizes the in-flight `createRuntime()` promise so concurrent callers share a single runtime. The promise is cleared in `_resetRuntime()` and on creation failure. \~12 line diff, no behaviour change outside the race.

Tested against our real deployment (3 stdio servers, one plain stdio + two via mcp-remote): before the fix a random subset of servers failed after every startup/reload; with this patch applied all servers register and tool calls succeed consistently.
